§6Ethanol§f §aSugar cane into fuel. Burns clean at 275 kTU and 687 kHE per bucket.§f §bEthanol§f is a flammable, combustible, polluting liquid (NFPA 2/3/0) with high fuel grade. One bucket provides §e275 kTU§f and §e687 kHE§f. §6Production§f:
§b• Chemical Plant§f (2.5s), 10× Sugar → 1,000 mB §eEthanol§f
§b• Industrial Liquefaction§f, Sugar → 100 mB, Mustard Willow → 50 mB, Hemp → 150 mB
§b• Combination Oven§f, Sugar Canes → 2 Sugar + 50 mB Ethanol §6Key Uses§f:
§b• §eBiofuel§f, Chemical Plant: 1,500 mB Biogas + 250 mB Ethanol → 1,000 mB Biofuel (3s)
§b• §eEngine Lubricant§f, Industrial Mixer: 200 mB Ethanol + 800 mB Fish Oil → 1,000 mB Lubricant
§b• §eCombustion Power§f, directly burn for HE or TU in appropriate generators §ePS:§f Sugar is renewable through sugar cane farming. Automate it, pipe sugar straight to a Chemical Plant, and you've got passive ethanol production. One stack of sugar yields roughly 6 buckets.
